news.title: Visa and Mastercard Settlement Awaits Ruling on Merchant Acceptance Changes
news.body: U.S. District Judge Brian Cogan ended the November 16 hearing on Visa and Mastercard’s proposed merchant settlement without ruling, PYMNTS reported. If approved, the proposal would give selected stores 90 days to revise rules for premium-card refusal pilots, limited to 180 days in a 12-month period. It would also cap posted interchange rates for standard consumer credit cards—not all cards—at 1.25% for eight years. Walmart, Circle K and the National Retail Federation oppose the settlement. Neither the proposed acceptance changes nor the interchange cap is effective yet.

news.title: Chase Reports Transaction Delays; Zelle Says Network Operations Remain Normal
news.body: Chase acknowledged an internal technical issue delaying some transactions on November 16, while saying customers retained access to accounts and funds and ruling out a cyberattack. Separately, U.S. Bank said its systems were unaffected but Zelle payments involving another institution could be delayed; the reporting does not identify that institution as Chase. Zelle reported normal network operations. Although customers reported problems at several banks, those complaints do not establish simultaneous bank outages or a shared infrastructure failure.

news.title: Stablecoin Supply Falls $12 Billion as Trading Balances Contract
news.body: Stablecoin market capitalization declined approximately $12 billion over 30 days, according to Bloomberg reporting summarized by PYMNTS. Kaiko’s Anastasia Melachrinos said USDT and USDC each contracted roughly 4%. The coverage places much of the contraction on exchanges and Ethereum, linking the decline to trading-related balances without establishing a fall in commercial stablecoin payments. For issuers, exchanges and redemption providers, the reported change concerns outstanding supply and trading liquidity; it does not measure merchant payment activity or settlement costs.

news.title: Apple Reportedly Selects Corey Fugman to Lead Pay and Wallet
news.body: Apple has selected Corey Fugman, a 26-year company veteran and senior director of Apple Pay and Wallet, to lead the unit, according to Bloomberg reporting summarized by PYMNTS. Jennifer Bailey is retiring and is expected to provide consulting support during the transition. Fugman has reportedly worked on the Apple Card partnership transition from Goldman Sachs to JPMorgan Chase. Apple declined Bloomberg’s request for comment. The personnel report includes no announced changes to merchant terms, wallet pricing or funding rails.

news.title: PayPal Treasury Case Study Reports Nearly Complete Cash Visibility
news.body: A Deutsche Bank case study covered PayPal’s management of $53 billion in corporate cash and customer funds across approximately 1,000 accounts and 160 currency pairs, PYMNTS reported. The company-reported results included cash visibility increasing from 78% to nearly 100% and cash-positioning accuracy exceeding 99%. A conversational AI agent sits above the consolidated treasury system, but the coverage does not isolate the agent’s contribution from the broader overhaul, disclose realized cost savings or establish autonomous fund movement.

perspective: Chase reports transaction delays, while PayPal’s treasury case study documents gains in cash visibility across roughly 1,000 accounts.

curiosity.text: Instant customer payments do not necessarily mean instant interbank settlement. The UK’s Faster Payments Service launched in 2008 using deferred multilateral net settlement: customers could receive payments within seconds while participating banks settled their net obligations later. Prefunding arrived in 2015 to cover those settlement obligations; it was not part of the original model and did not turn each customer payment into a separate real-time central-bank settlement. Source: Bank of England, Annual Report and Accounts 2015–16 — https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/annual-report/2016
